newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH ZLOTY EASES VS BASKET, TAX PAYMENTS UP O/N.
newsitem.headline: POLISH ZLOTY EASES VS BASKET, TAX PAYMENTS UP O/N.

text.p: The Polish zloty eased against the trading band centre in live trade on Thursday as banks rebuilt currency positions shortened earlier this week, but dealers were mixed on whether zloty-buying will continue.
They said speculation propelled trade in the absence of client orders today and that currency-buying was supported by the dollar's rebound against the mark on world markets.

"After a high opening, active speculative trade and currency-buying dominated Thursday's session, but the market is not sure whether the trend will continue on Friday, as it is not client based," said Pawel Gajewski from Creditanstalt.
The Polish zloty closed down at 2.09/2.06 percent against the trading band centre from Wednesday's 2.17/2.14 percent.
It was at 2.8115/25 to the dollar, down from Wednesday's 2.8055/65 and at 1.8707/15 to the mark, flat from 1.8710/15.

On the money market players reported high volatility in overnight rates, which jumped some 0.6 point in early trade before edging down again as November's monthly tax payment outflows created additional demand on Thursday.
"This month firms pay monthly taxes for November and prepay December's tax, which created additional demand for cash," said Malgorzata Sikora of ING bank in Warsaw.
Overnight rates were at 18.75/19.05 percent, up from 18.6/18.8, and tomorrow/next at 18.85/19.15 versus 19.0/19.15.

Yields on the secondary T-bill market were unmoved despite the lower house's Thursday decision to keep three tax levels in 1997 as foreigners remained sidelined after disappointing October inflation figures, dealers said. One-year bills, sold on Monday at 19.53, were traded at 19.55/50 percent.
Dealers said foreign investors would not become a factor in secondary trade until talk of an interest or exchange rate policy change starts, which right now was out of the question.
